The game is perfect for scratching that Skyrim itch that you had for years, aside from actually playing Skyrim (game still holds to this day!). The game in itself is in early access but it incorporated every good bits and pieces of other good games into one viking setting. The game is pretty enjoyable played alone, but its so good to play with friends. I recommend to play it coop so you'll enjoy it a lot. The problem with the game right now is the fps reduction and some lags during a few points in the game, but its manageable if you have decent graphics card and processor. I definitely recommend it to everyone!

Well put together mix of survival, crafting and combat. Worth the play through and for those whom like to complete epic builds and test your metal, this is for you. Also, you are able to play 100% solo or with friends. No difference. Update 2023 September.

Better with friends but enjoyable when playing solo as well. Very good buy. I'm going to blunt; This is the best game I have played in 10 years. Hands down. No contest.
I have over 700hrs in on this game and I still find myself daydreaming when I'm not at home what I'm going to do in game later.
Me and my wife love this game to bits, while also breaking down the mechanics into little bits.
Even after acquiring a deep understanding of the games mechanics and breaking the game for speed-runs, I can still crack open a beer with 4 or 5 friends and smack rocks and punch boars and forget whats needed for a tanning rack.
Its really the perfect game.

When I got this game I was prepared for at least a 10 GB file, you can imagine my surprise when I was presented with only 1 GB. I haven't put an extreme amount of hours in yet but that will definitely change. The graphics paired with the soundtrack and story ties the whole thing together beautifully. A very good change of pace from my usual list of games. I'm very excited to see where the devs decide to go next.

Ok, let's say it started the genre... Ok, let's admit there are some moments of excitement... But I don't quite see the point in playing this game in 2026! There are just better games available for every aspect: better combat, better building, better crafting, better graphics for god sake! Procedural world feels unengaging, combat is clunky, exploration is less about "exploring" but more of traversal of the same landscape again and again. And above all... F****G GRIND! And the worst part is that it is about grinding trees and stones in different bioms over and over again. Probably the only mode for playing this game is while listening to a podcast.

The procedurally generated worlds, high difficulty, and comparatively unforgiving game mechanics succeed at creating a feeling of danger and adventure many modern games lack. Combined with the excellent lighting, environmental effects and sound, the overall vibe and atmosphere of the game is its biggest strength.

There are no doubt many mechanics that will have you raging and ready to throw your computer out the window. But I honestly don't know if the game works without them. The highs aren't as high without the lows. Its a tightrope Valheim walks well enough to stand out as a unique and overall enjoyable gaming experience.

This game is fantastic! Enjoy an epic journey through the viking afterlife! Building in this game is so satisfying. If this game stopped development right now I would still be more than pleased with my purchase. Luckily we still have Ashlands coming out by the first half of this year TM, and Deep North after that. I'm sure I will sink another 400 hours or so in to it. The replay ability is great whether solo or with friends. As I write this the game is on sale for $11.00. I highly recommend anyone who is even remotely interested pick it up!

Immersive, brutal, beautiful <3

Valheim is one of my all time favorites. I’ve only experienced the game with friends, never solo, and honestly, our co-op adventure was legendary! Exploring unknown lands, sailing across oceans, building our fort together, every moment was an absolute blast.

Each biome is beautiful in its own way, even the most brutal ones. The building system is really spot on and fits the medieval aesthetic perfectly (especially proud of our base - Viking’s Landing). The combat is solid overall, though I do wish bosses had more variety in their attacks. That said, the best part about this game is the co-op journey! If you ever consider trying this game, I heavily recommend playing with friends!

Brutally honest short-ish review: The last time i had fun on this game was when i was born. If you've never played this game, its a great play with friends for about a week given you play daily. Its amazing the first go-round. But for someone who played this for about 60 or so hours and have done everything there is to do in that short amount of time, the game isn't updating fast enough. The H&H update was absolute garbage, added nothing, and isn't anything short from a hotfix. This update was for people who never stopped playing the game since February or months on end since launch, however that is possible.. The fact that this was hyped up is appalling. They spent millions of $ hiring some artist to design the visual graphic of the roadmap and not even a thousand worth in work hours designing the update. 8 months later.. come on.

TLDR: devs cannot grasp any concept of timely updates and are failing to keep the game alive regardless of whether its in alpha or not. Updates take a full year to add 1 wall and 12 new items of food while also making the food mechanics WORSE. Awesome.

Amazing open world survival/crafting game. Highly recommend playing with friends as it's very difficult by yourself. Once you get the hang of it you can craft amazing gear and portals and ships and the map is MASSIVE and takes literal days/weeks to explore even with more than one player. Still being constantly updated by developers with a new release just last month adding even more content to the already content-rich game. Some players go so far as to draw out literal maps on paper or in other apps to help with locating/remembering areas. Well worth the $29.99 price tag but also look for sales as sometimes the game can be as cheap as $9.99 which is more than worth it for the amount of content the game offers. Also, the game doesn't take a high-end gaming PC or anything like that to run which is nice in itself, most laptops can even handle it if you want to play while traveling or anything like that. Great game overall, I'd give it a solid 8-9 out of 10 any day of the week as at time it can be frustratingly difficult but brought me lots joy playing with my girlfriend and other friends, building huge bases, and offering nearly endless exploration.
